user_profile.other_preferences: Need remote job, prepare for global market, Basic (Completed some courses / small exercises) coding experience, familiar with python,C++,C languages. Also build some academic projects. Preferable programming language is Python

prompt_used:
I want to become a Computer Vision Engineer. I have 6 months to prepare and I can study 4 hours per day. 
My experience level is University Final Year CSE Student. Need remote job, prepare for global market, Basic (Completed some courses / small exercises) coding experience, familiar with python,C++,C languages. Also build some academic projects. Preferable programming language is Python
Now generate a learning plan for me.

generated_plan.title: 6-Month Learning Plan for Computer Vision Engineer (Remote/Global Market)

plan.focus: Foundations: Math, Python for Data Science, ML Basics & Version Control

topics: Python Refresher & Advanced Topics (Generators, Decorators, OOP)
NumPy & Pandas for data manipulation
Git & GitHub essentials (commits, branches, pull requests)
activities: Solve Python exercises (e.g., HackerRank, LeetCode Easy)
Practice NumPy array operations and Pandas DataFrame manipulations
Set up a GitHub profile and create a basic repository

topics: Mathematical Foundations for ML: Linear Algebra (vectors, matrices, dot products)
Mathematical Foundations for ML: Calculus (derivatives, gradients)
Mathematical Foundations for ML: Probability & Statistics (distributions, mean, variance)
activities: Review relevant math concepts with focus on ML applications
Solve practice problems related to linear algebra and calculus for ML
Understand statistical concepts through examples
resources: Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng (Coursera - Math refreshers)

topics: Introduction to Machine Learning (Supervised vs. Unsupervised, Regression, Classification)
Scikit-learn basics (data loading, splitting, model training, evaluation)
Linear Regression & Logistic Regression
activities: Implement Linear and Logistic Regression from scratch using NumPy
Train and evaluate models using Scikit-learn on simple datasets (e.g., Iris)
Understand bias-variance trade-off
resources: Machine Learning by Andrew Ng (Coursera - theoretical foundation)
Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow (Chapter 1-4)

topics: Introduction to Jupyter Notebooks/Labs
Matplotlib & Seaborn for data visualization
Evaluation Metrics for Classification and Regression (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, MSE, R-squared)
activities: Create visualizations for ML model results
Analyze and interpret different evaluation metrics
Work on a small end-to-end ML project (e.g., predicting house prices using a simple model)
resources: Kaggle tutorials (Data Visualization, Intro to ML)

plan.focus: Core Computer Vision (Traditional CV) with OpenCV

topics: Image Fundamentals: Pixels, Color Spaces (RGB, Grayscale, HSV)
Image Operations: Resizing, Cropping, Rotation, Flipping
Image Filtering: Convolution, Blurring (Gaussian, Median), Sharpening
activities: Load, display, and manipulate images using OpenCV-Python
Apply various filters and observe their effects on images
Implement a simple convolution filter from scratch
resources: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications (Szeliski) - Chapter 3

topics: Edge Detection: Sobel, Canny operators
Morphological Operations: Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing
Contour Detection & Analysis
activities: Detect edges in images using Canny
Apply morphological operations for noise reduction and shape analysis
Find and draw contours, calculate properties (area, perimeter)

topics: Feature Detection: Harris Corner Detector, FAST, SIFT, SURF (conceptual understanding)
Feature Descriptors: HOG, ORB
Feature Matching: Brute-Force Matcher, FLANN Matcher
activities: Extract features using ORB and HOG
Perform feature matching between two images to find correspondences
Implement a simple object recognition based on feature matching

topics: Object Tracking: Mean Shift, CamShift, optical flow (Lucas-Kanade)
Basic Geometric Vision: Homography, Image Warping
Introduction to Image Stitching/Panoramas
activities: Implement a basic object tracking system using optical flow
Perform image warping and homography transformations
Attempt a simple image stitching project
resources: Kaggle project ideas for traditional CV

plan.focus: Deep Learning Fundamentals & CNNs for Image Classification

topics: Introduction to Neural Networks: Perceptron, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)
Activation Functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax)
Loss Functions (Cross-Entropy, MSE)
Backpropagation Algorithm
activities: Implement a simple Perceptron from scratch
Understand the math behind backpropagation
Practice forward and backward passes conceptually
resources: Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng (Coursera) - Course 1 (Neural Networks and Deep Learning)
Neural Networks and Deep Learning by Michael Nielsen (online book)

topics: Deep Learning Frameworks: PyTorch (tensors, autograd, nn.Module)
Optimizers (SGD, Adam, RMSprop)
Regularization (L1, L2, Dropout)
activities: Set up PyTorch development environment
Implement a simple MLP for classification using PyTorch
Experiment with different optimizers and regularization techniques
resources: PyTorch Official Tutorials (Deep Learning with PyTorch: A 60 Minute Blitz)

topics: Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs): Convolutional Layer, Pooling Layer
CNN Architectures: LeNet-5, AlexNet, VGG
Understanding receptive fields and feature maps
activities: Implement a simple CNN for MNIST digit classification using PyTorch
Experiment with different kernel sizes, strides, and pooling operations
Visualize feature maps (conceptual)
resources: Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng - Course 4 (Convolutional Neural Networks)
CS231n Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition (Stanford lectures)

topics: Advanced CNN Architectures: ResNet, Inception, MobileNet (conceptual)
Transfer Learning: Fine-tuning pre-trained models
Data Augmentation techniques for images
activities: Train an image classifier on a small dataset (e.g., CIFAR-10) using a pre-trained model (e.g., ResNet-18) with transfer learning
Implement various data augmentation strategies
Analyze model performance with and without transfer learning/augmentation

plan.focus: Advanced Deep Learning for Computer Vision (Object Detection & Segmentation)

topics: Introduction to Object Detection: Bounding Boxes, IoU, NMS
Two-Stage Detectors: R-CNN, Fast R-CNN, Faster R-CNN (conceptual understanding)
One-Stage Detectors: YOLO family (v1-v3 basics), SSD
activities: Understand the workflow of object detection models
Use a pre-trained YOLO model (e.g., from PyTorch Hub) to detect objects in images/videos
Explore COCO dataset format
resources: Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng - Course 4 (Object Detection)
PyTorch Hub models (e.g., YOLOv5/YOLOv8 from Ultralytics)

topics: Practical Object Detection with YOLOv5/v8 (training custom datasets)
Evaluating Object Detection Models: mAP (Mean Average Precision)
Introduction to Instance Segmentation (Mask R-CNN conceptual)
activities: Gather a small custom dataset and train a YOLOv5/v8 model for a specific object
Understand and calculate mAP for a detection task
Run inference with a pre-trained Mask R-CNN model

topics: Introduction to Semantic Segmentation: FCN, U-Net
Loss functions for Segmentation (Dice Loss, Focal Loss)
Data preparation for segmentation tasks
activities: Implement a basic U-Net architecture (or use a library implementation)
Train a semantic segmentation model on a simple dataset (e.g., PASCAL VOC segmentation task)
Evaluate segmentation masks (IoU/Jaccard Index)

topics: Introduction to Pose Estimation (Keypoint detection - conceptual)
Generative Models in CV (GANs - basic idea, applications)
Introduction to Vision Transformers (ViT - conceptual)
activities: Explore pre-trained pose estimation models (e.g., OpenPose, AlphaPose)
Understand the high-level concept of GANs and their use cases (e.g., image generation)
Read introductory blogs on Vision Transformers
resources: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) by Ian Goodfellow (original paper/blog posts)

plan.focus: Practical Application, Project Building & Deployment Basics

topics: End-to-end Project Planning: Problem definition, data collection/annotation strategy
Data Preprocessing & Augmentation Best Practices for complex datasets
Experiment Tracking & Management (MLflow/Weights & Biases - basic usage)
activities: Select a challenging CV project (e.g., custom object detection for a niche, face recognition system)
Start collecting/curating data for the chosen project
Set up MLflow for tracking experiments
resources: Medium articles on ML project structure

topics: Model Optimization: Quantization (conceptual), pruning (conceptual), ONNX
Introduction to Model Deployment: REST APIs (Flask/FastAPI)
Containerization with Docker for ML applications
activities: Convert a PyTorch model to ONNX format
Build a simple Flask/FastAPI endpoint to serve a pre-trained CV model (e.g., image classifier)
Create a Dockerfile for your model serving application

topics: Cloud Deployment Concepts: AWS Sagemaker, GCP AI Platform, Azure ML (high-level overview)
Monitoring & MLOps basics (Data drift, model drift - conceptual)
Refining and optimizing the chosen CV project
activities: Explore the capabilities of one cloud ML platform (e.g., create an AWS free tier account and check Sagemaker)
Continue working on the main CV project, focusing on improving performance and robustness
Document the project thoroughly
resources: Research papers related to your chosen project

topics: Participate in a Kaggle Computer Vision competition (even if just for learning)
Code quality, testing, and documentation for ML projects
Advanced Git practices (rebase, squashing commits)
activities: Actively participate in a Kaggle competition, learning from others' approaches
Refactor project code, add unit tests, and improve documentation
Review and refine your main CV project to make it portfolio-ready

plan.focus: Job Preparation: Portfolio, Resume, Interview Skills & LeetCode

topics: Portfolio Development: Showcase projects on GitHub (READMEs, clear code, demos)
Creating a Personal Website/Blog (optional but recommended for global market)
Resume/CV Preparation: Tailoring for Computer Vision Engineer roles
activities: Curate your best projects, write compelling READMEs with results and insights
Build a simple personal website to host your portfolio and blog posts
Draft and refine your resume, highlighting CV/ML skills and projects
resources: Examples of good ML engineer portfolios

topics: Coding Interview Preparation: Data Structures & Algorithms (LeetCode Medium)
System Design Interview Basics (for ML/CV systems)
Behavioral Interview Questions
activities: Solve LeetCode Medium problems focusing on common DS&A
Study common ML system design questions (e.g., 'design a face recognition system')
Practice answering behavioral questions (STAR method)
resources: Grokking the System Design Interview (online course)

topics: Review of Core Computer Vision & Deep Learning Concepts
Latest trends in CV (read recent papers/blogs)
Networking: LinkedIn profile optimization, reaching out to recruiters
activities: Revisit weak areas from previous months, consolidate knowledge
Stay updated with recent advancements in CV via ArXiv, popular blogs, Twitter
Optimize LinkedIn profile, start connecting with recruiters and CV engineers

topics: Mock Interviews (Technical, System Design, Behavioral)
Application Strategy: Identifying target companies & roles
Final Portfolio Review & polishing
activities: Conduct mock interviews with peers or mentors
Start applying for remote Computer Vision Engineer/ML Engineer roles
Ensure all portfolio projects are impeccable and well-documented
resources: Job boards (LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed, specialized remote job boards)
